Subject: Syndicated storage connector / co-sell integration — proposal and next steps

Hi Sam / Pinecone partnerships team,

Thanks again for the discussion last week — we left with strong alignment that a lightweight connector (Redwood <-> Pinecone) plus a co-sell / GTM pilot could surface good demand for both sides. I sketched a pragmatic two-phase approach below and attached a short tech outline for your engs to review.

High level proposal (phase-focused):
- Phase 1 (30-day pilot): simple index connector that allows our hosted API customers to choose Pinecone as a vector store fallback; routing and billing handled by Redwood. Minimal schema mapping + autosync of embeddings.
- Phase 2 (90-day co-sell pilot): joint GTM (one playbook), marketplace listing on both sides, and a rev-share/referral model for conversions.

Open asks for your team:
1) Security/controls checklist — do you require SOC2 evidence or separate attestations for index read/write flows?
2) Data residency constraints — can Pinecone support region pinning for customer indices during the pilot?
3) Technical ownership — who will own adapter maintenance and major releases?

Attached: tech_spec_outline.pdf (very light, API contract + sync patterns).

If this looks good, can we aim to:
- Confirm security checklist by EOD next Wed (5/17)
- Legal: exchange a short MOU for commercial terms by 5/24
- Technical kickoff week of 5/29 (30–60 min)

Thanks — I can host the kickoff and loop in solutions if you want.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
Diego | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Syndicated storage connector / co-sell integration — proposal and next steps

Diego — great summary, appreciate the pragmatic split. Quick answers and a few follow-ups below.

Short answers:
- Security: yes, we will need a copy of Redwood's SOC2 report and a brief architecture diagram showing where embeddings and metadata reside (we treat provider-hosted user indices as critical).
- Residency: we can pin indices to region (us-east, eu-west) for pilot customers; can confirm isolation requirements for specific enterprise accounts.
- Ownership: Pinecone prefers maintaining the SDK/adapter for index lifecycle (backups, TTL policies) while Redwood owns the runtime integration and routing. We can be flexible.

Follow-ups:
1) I'll share our integration checklist (attaching pinecone-integration-checklist.xlsx) — please fill where relevant.
2) For commercial terms, partners@pinecone.io handles MOU + rev-share templates. Can we get an initial ask from your side (referral % or suggested split)?
3) Security contact: loop in legal-security@pinecone.io; they will want to run a short questionnaire.

We like your timeline. I can commit to a technical kickoff the week of 5/29 — Wed or Thu preferred.

Best,
Sam Park
Head of Partnerships, Pinecone
